title: Chemoselectivity: NaBH₄ reduces a ketone, not an ester
caption: Sodium borohydride is a mild hydride donor: it reduces the ketone of methyl 4-oxopentanoate to a secondary alcohol but leaves the less electrophilic ester untouched. LiAlH₄ would reduce both.
alt: Methyl 4-oxopentanoate, an arrow labelled NaBH₄, and methyl 4-hydroxypentanoate; the ketone and the new alcohol are shaded, the ester unchanged.
description: Starting material: a ketone and an ester in one molecule.
After NaBH₄: the ketone has become a secondary alcohol; the ester is unchanged.
